questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A quiz question asks: what is the structure of a triglyceride?

options.text: A glycerol with one fatty acid
A glycerol esterified with three fatty acids
A chain of three amino acids
A phosphate with two fatty acids

questions.explanation: A triglyceride is formed by esterifying the three hydroxyl groups of glycerol with three long-chain fatty acids, serving as the main storage form of energy in adipose tissue.
questions.hint: Glycerol plus three fatty acids by ester bonds.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the sample reaction, what products form when a triglyceride is hydrolyzed with aqueous base?

options.text: Glycerol and free fatty acids only
options.misconception: base gives salts of the acids

questions.explanation: Base hydrolysis of a triglyceride cleaves the three ester bonds to give glycerol and three fatty acid carboxylate salts, which are soaps; this is the process of saponification.
questions.hint: Base gives glycerol plus fatty acid salts.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: During a lab exercise, what structural feature makes a phospholipid amphipathic?

options.text: A polar phosphate head and nonpolar hydrocarbon tails

questions.explanation: A phospholipid has a hydrophilic polar phosphate-containing head and two hydrophobic hydrocarbon tails, so it spontaneously forms bilayers in water with heads outward and tails inward.
questions.hint: Polar head plus nonpolar tails gives amphipathic behavior.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a problem set, what is the core structure of a steroid?

options.text: Four fused rings with three six-membered and one five-membered
A chain of four amino acids

questions.explanation: Steroids share a fused tetracyclic ring system of three cyclohexane rings and one cyclopentane ring, with substituents and unsaturation distinguishing individual steroids such as cholesterol.
questions.hint: Three six-membered and one five-membered fused rings.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Testing your understanding: which sugar is present in DNA?

options.misconception: glucose is not in nucleic acids
fructose is not in nucleic acids

questions.explanation: DNA contains the five-carbon sugar 2-deoxyribose, which lacks a hydroxyl at the 2-prime position, while RNA contains ribose with a 2-prime hydroxyl that makes RNA more susceptible to hydrolysis.
questions.hint: DNA has deoxyribose; RNA has ribose.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.learningObjective: Count hydrogen bonds in base pairs
questions.stem: A problem asks: how many hydrogen bonds form between adenine and thymine in DNA?

options.misconception: G-C pairs have three hydrogen bonds
base pairs use two or three

questions.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, while guanine pairs with cytosine through three, which is why GC-rich DNA has a higher melting temperature.
questions.hint: A-T has two; G-C has three.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: An examiner asks: what linkage joins adjacent nucleotides in a nucleic acid?

options.misconception: bases attach to the sugar by glycosidic bonds but nucleotides are linked by phosphate

options.text: A phosphodiester bond between the 3-prime and 5-prime carbons

questions.explanation: Nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester bonds in which a phosphate group links the 3-prime hydroxyl of one sugar to the 5-prime hydroxyl of the next, forming the directional backbone of DNA and RNA.
questions.hint: Phosphate bridges 3-prime and 5-prime carbons.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a handout exercise, which nitrogenous base is found in RNA but not in DNA?
questions.explanation: RNA uses uracil in place of thymine, so its base set is adenine, guanine, cytosine and uracil, while DNA uses adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine.
questions.hint: Uracil replaces thymine in RNA.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: Applying the mechanism, which property distinguishes a saturated fatty acid from an unsaturated one?

options.text: The absence of carbon-carbon double bonds
The presence of a phosphate group

questions.explanation: A saturated fatty acid has no carbon-carbon double bonds in its hydrocarbon chain and packs tightly, giving a higher melting point, while unsaturated fatty acids contain double bonds that introduce kinks and lower melting points.
questions.hint: Saturated means no double bonds.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: As a check, what is meant by antiparallel strands in DNA?

options.text: Both strands run in the same direction
One strand runs 5-prime to 3-prime while the other runs 3-prime to 5-prime
The strands are covalently joined along their length
options.misconception: they are held by hydrogen bonds

questions.explanation: The two DNA strands run in opposite directions, with one oriented 5-prime to 3-prime and the complementary strand 3-prime to 5-prime, which is required for the specific hydrogen bonding of the double helix.
questions.hint: Antiparallel means opposite 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

questions.hint: Antiparallel means opposite 5-prime to 3-prime direction.
